title: Weighted universal Value-at-Risk Superadditivity for discrete distributions
summary: The concept of weighted universal Value-at-Risk superadditivity (WUVS) was recently introduced by Chen et al. (2026) as a generalization of the question whether for some infinite mean distributions convex combinations of i.i.d. random variables can stochastically dominate the parent distribution. In this short note we prove that the property WUVS can basically never hold for discrete distributions except for the case of comonotonicity.
